questions.question: MATS (ML Alignment & Theory Scholars) functions primarily as what type of organization?
options: A government-funded research institute that publishes foundational alignment papers
A research mentorship program that trains alignment researchers and feeds them into frontier labs and external evaluation organizations
A certification body that audits AI safety claims from frontier labs
A venture capital fund that invests in AI safety startups
questions.explanation: MATS is a research mentorship program: scholars spend 10-12 weeks with senior researchers on alignment problems. The key role is talent development — approximately 80% of pre-2025 alumni work on safety/security, with 200+ at Anthropic, DeepMind, OpenAI, UK AISI, Redwood, METR, and Apollo.

questions.question: Redwood Research's primary methodological style is characterized by:
options: Theoretical proofs about worst-case model behavior
Specific threat models, worst-case adversaries, and concrete protocols that can be stress-tested — applied alignment rather than theoretical
Large-scale empirical studies measuring alignment properties across many models
Policy analysis and recommendation of governance structures
questions.explanation: Redwood Research (founded by Buck Shlegeris) focuses on applied alignment: specific threat models (adversarially optimizing U), worst-case adversaries, and concrete deployable protocols. AI Control (Lesson 10) exemplifies this style: the threat model is explicit, the protocol is specified, and it is tested against red-team pressure.

questions.question: Apollo Research specializes in which type of pre-deployment evaluation?
options: Capability benchmarking across standard academic tasks
Scheming evaluations — agentic settings where deception can emerge from in-context goal conflicts
Privacy audits measuring training data memorization
Fairness evaluations measuring demographic parity across model outputs
questions.explanation: Apollo Research conducts pre-deployment scheming evaluations for frontier labs. Their canonical work (In-Context Scheming, Lesson 8) tests agentic scenarios where models can develop scheming behavior from in-context goal conflicts. Their methodological style uses the three-pillar decomposition: misalignment, goal-directedness, situational awareness.

questions.question: METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) is primarily known for what type of evaluation?
options: Jailbreak evaluations measuring attack success rates
Task-based capability evaluations including autonomous-task time-horizon studies
Privacy audits and data extraction measurements
Bias evaluations across demographic groups
questions.explanation: METR focuses on task-based capability evaluations and autonomous-task time-horizon studies — measuring how far a model can progress on complex multi-step tasks without human intervention. They also produce framework synthesis documents like 'Common Elements of Frontier AI Safety Policies' that compare across labs.

questions.question: Why is the multi-organizational structure (labs + external evaluators) described as the quality control mechanism for alignment research?
options: Multiple organizations produce more papers, increasing the chance of discovering important results

Labs have a structural conflict of interest evaluating their own models; external evaluators can raise and validate failure modes that labs may underreport — the multi-org structure provides independent verification
Government regulations require independent evaluation before deployment
External evaluators use different hardware that can detect failure modes invisible to lab infrastructure
questions.explanation: Single-source evaluations are structurally unreliable when the evaluator is the model's producer. The 2024 canonical papers illustrate this: Sleeper Agents (Anthropic + Redwood), Alignment Faking (Anthropic + Redwood), In-Context Scheming (Apollo alone), Anti-Scheming (Apollo + OpenAI). The multi-org structure ensures critical findings have independent endorsement.

questions.question: Eleos AI Research occupies a unique niche in the ecosystem. What is it?
options: The only organization that publishes adversarial jailbreak attack papers
The only organization focused on model-welfare pre-deployment evaluations, providing external methodology checks for welfare-relevant claims
The primary training-data audit organization that verifies data provenance claims
The certification body for GPAI Code of Practice compliance
questions.explanation: Eleos AI Research is described as the only pure model-welfare organization in the ecosystem. They conducted the Claude Opus 4 welfare assessment documented in the system card (Lesson 19) and provide external methodology checks for welfare-relevant claims — in particular, the caveat about model self-reports being sensitive to user expectations.
